fullPassage:
Welcome back to Today's Health. Today we're going to be talking about exercise. Dr. Victoria Hill is here, and she is going to share some useful tips. So, Dr. Hill, let's start with a question about my experience last month. I worked out right after dinner and got a stomachache. Why did that happen?

Well, the problem is that you exercised too soon after eating. This can cause various stomach issues. When you eat, blood rushes to the digestive system to help break down the food and absorb its nutrients. But when you start to exercise, blood moves from the digestive system to your muscles. This happens in order to supply your muscles with the oxygen and nutrients they require. As a result, the digestion process is paused until the blood returns. So, whether you're lifting weights or going for a jog, you shouldn't do it with a stomach full of food.

I see. That makes sense. So, does that mean I should exercise on an empty stomach?

No, it doesn't. That can also be harmful and unpleasant. This is because the body needs energy to exercise. The fuel that provides this energy is glycogen. Carbohydrates in the food we eat are broken down into a kind of sugar called glucose. When this glucose is stored in parts of the body, such as the muscles and the liver, it is called glycogen. This is why exercising on a completely empty stomach — such as when you first wake up in the morning — can be such a challenge. Your blood sugar levels are low, and you don't have enough glycogen stored in your body. If you exercise on an empty stomach, you will most likely lack energy and feel unusually tired. There can also be more serious outcomes. Some people end up suffering from nausea and headaches, and others even faint. This is because intense exercise uses up all the glycogen in your muscles.

So, is it the loss of glycogen that causes us to have low levels of energy?

That's correct. For this reason, doctors recommend that people eat food containing carbohydrates within thirty minutes after working out. This replaces the muscle glycogen you have lost. Basically, you need between one and one and a half grams of carbohydrates for every kilogram you weigh. Let's do the math. If you weigh 60 kilograms, you should try to consume between 60 and 90 grams of carbohydrates after you exercise. This is equal to about one bowl of white rice or three bananas.

That's very interesting. But what about eating before we exercise? Can you explain how long we should wait after eating?

Well, as I said before, exercising right after you eat will cause feelings of discomfort. But, if you wait too long to exercise after eating, you'll suffer from a lack of energy. The best time to eat before you exercise varies from one to three hours. Basically, it depends on several factors such as the type and amount of food as well as body size, age, and gender. The type of exercise also matters. For extremely active exercise like cycling, I suggest that you wait between one and a half and three hours after eating a moderate-sized meal. But for something more casual, such as golfing, waiting for one hour after a meal should be enough. Clearly, you can wait less after eating a snack.

Thank you very much for this fascinating information, Dr. Hill. I'm sure it will be very helpful for all of our viewers.

questions.passage: When you eat, blood rushes to the (A)[digestive / nervous] system to help break down the food and (B)[absorb / release] its nutrients. But when you start to exercise, blood moves from the digestive system to your muscles. This happens in order to (C)[supply / deprive] your muscles with the oxygen and nutrients they require.
questions.stem: 위 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 식사할 때 혈액은 음식을 분해하고 영양분을 흡수하기 위해 소화 기관으로 움직인다. 운동하면 근육에 산소와 영양분을 공급하기 위해 혈액이 이동한다.
det.analysis:
✅ (A) digestive: 소화 기관. nervous(신경)는 부적합.
✅ (B) absorb: 영양분을 흡수. release(방출)는 반대.
✅ (C) supply: 공급하다. deprive(박탈하다)는 반대.
det.tip: digestive system: 소화 기관 / absorb nutrients: 영양분을 흡수하다 / supply A with B: A에 B를 공급하다

questions.passage: Exercising on an empty stomach can also be (A)[harmful / beneficial] and unpleasant. This is because the body needs energy to exercise. The fuel that provides this energy is glycogen. If you exercise on an empty stomach, you will most likely (B)[lack / gain] energy and feel unusually tired. Some people end up suffering from nausea and headaches, and others even (C)[faint / recover].
questions.stem: 위 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈속에 운동하는 것은 해롭고 불쾌할 수 있다. 에너지가 부족하고 피곤해진다. 어떤 사람들은 실신하기도 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ (A) harmful: 빈속 운동은 '해롭다'. beneficial(유익한)은 반대.
✅ (B) lack: 에너지 '부족'. gain(얻다)은 반대.
✅ (C) faint: '실신'한다. recover(회복하다)는 반대.
det.tip: harmful(해로운) ↔ beneficial(유익한) / lack(부족하다) ↔ gain(얻다) / faint(실신하다)

questions.passage: The best time to eat before you exercise (A)[varies / remains] from one to three hours. Basically, it depends on several factors such as the type and amount of food as well as body size, age, and gender. The type of exercise also (B)[matters / disappears]. For extremely active exercise like cycling, I suggest that you wait between one and a half and three hours after eating a (C)[moderate / excessive]-sized meal.
questions.stem: 위 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 운동 전 식사 시간은 1~3시간으로 다르다. 운동 종류도 중요하다. 적정량의 식사 후 기다려라.
det.analysis:
✅ (A) varies: 1~3시간으로 '다르다(varies)'. remains(유지되다)는 부적합.
✅ (B) matters: '중요하다'. disappears(사라지다)는 무관.
✅ (C) moderate: '적정량의'. excessive(과도한)는 부적합.
det.tip: vary from A to B: A에서 B까지 다르다 / matter: 중요하다 / moderate-sized: 적정 크기의

questions.passage: When you eat, blood rushes to the digestive system to help break down the food and absorb its ①<u>nutrients</u>. But when you start to exercise, blood moves from the digestive system to your ②<u>muscles</u>. As a result, the digestion process is ③<u>paused</u> until the blood returns. So, you shouldn't do it with a stomach ④<u>empty</u> of food.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 혈액은 음식의 ①영양분을 흡수하기 위해 소화 기관으로 간다. 운동하면 ②근육으로 이동한다. 소화 과정은 ③중단된다. 위장에 음식이 ④비어있는 채로 하면 안 된다.
det.analysis:
✅ ①②③ 원문 그대로.
❌ ④ empty(비어있는) → 원문은 full(가득한). 'a stomach full of food(음식이 가득한 위)'가 맞음.
det.tip: full of food(음식이 가득한) ↔ empty of food(비어있는) / 식후 운동 금지 맥락

questions.passage: Carbohydrates in the food we eat are broken down into a kind of sugar called glucose. When this glucose is ①<u>stored</u> in parts of the body, such as the muscles and the liver, it is called glycogen. If you exercise on an empty stomach, you will most likely ②<u>lack</u> energy and feel unusually tired. This is because intense exercise ③<u>uses up</u> all the glycogen in your muscles. For this reason, doctors ④<u>discourage</u> that people eat food containing carbohydrates within thirty minutes after working out.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 글루코스가 ①저장되면 글리코겐이라 한다. 빈속 운동은 에너지 ②부족. 강한 운동이 글리코겐을 ③다 써버린다. 의사들은 탄수화물 섭취를 ④권장하지 않는다.
det.analysis:
✅ ①②③ 원문 그대로.
❌ ④ discourage(권장하지 않다) → 원문은 recommend(권장하다). 의사들은 운동 후 탄수화물 섭취를 '권장'한다.
det.tip: recommend(권장하다) ↔ discourage(권장하지 않다, 만류하다)

questions.passage: Exercising right after you eat will cause feelings of ①<u>discomfort</u>. But, if you wait too long to exercise after eating, you'll suffer from a lack of energy. The best time to eat before you exercise varies from one to three hours. Basically, it ②<u>depends</u> on several factors such as the type and amount of food as well as body size, age, and gender. The type of exercise also ③<u>matters</u>. For extremely ④<u>passive</u> exercise like cycling, I suggest that you wait between one and a half and three hours.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 식사 직후 운동은 ①불편함을 유발한다. 여러 요소에 ②달려 있다. 운동 종류도 ③중요하다. 사이클링 같은 매우 ④수동적인 운동.
det.analysis:
✅ ①②③ 원문 그대로.
❌ ④ passive(수동적인) → 원문은 active(활동적인). cycling은 '매우 활동적인' 운동.
⚠️ 함정: passive는 운동 맥락에서 가능해 보이지만, cycling은 대표적인 고강도 운동.
det.tip: active(활동적인) ↔ passive(수동적인) / extremely active exercise: 매우 활동적인 운동

questions.passage: This is because the body needs energy to exercise. The fuel that provides this energy is glycogen. Carbohydrates in the food we eat are broken down into a kind of sugar called __________. When this sugar is stored in parts of the body, it is called glycogen.
questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 탄수화물은 글루코스(포도당)라고 불리는 일종의 당분으로 분해된다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② glucose: 탄수화물 → 글루코스(포도당)로 분해.
❌ ① protein(단백질): 탄수화물 분해 산물 아님.
❌ ③ vitamin(비타민): 무관.
❌ ④ mineral(무기질): 무관.
det.tip: glucose(글루코스, 포도당): 탄수화물이 분해되어 만들어지는 당분

questions.passage: For this reason, doctors recommend that people eat food containing carbohydrates within thirty minutes after working out. This replaces the muscle glycogen you have lost. Basically, you need between one and one and a half grams of carbohydrates for every kilogram you weigh. If you weigh 60 kilograms, you should try to __________ between 60 and 90 grams of carbohydrates after you exercise.
questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 60kg이라면 운동 후 60~90g의 탄수화물을 섭취하려고 노력해야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② consume: '섭취하다'. 운동 후 탄수화물 보충 맥락.
❌ ① avoid(피하다): 반대.
❌ ③ eliminate(제거하다): 반대.
❌ ④ reduce(줄이다): 반대.
det.tip: consume: 섭취하다, 소비하다 / consume carbohydrates: 탄수화물을 섭취하다

questions.passage: Exercising right after you eat will cause feelings of discomfort. But, if you wait too long to exercise after eating, you'll suffer from a lack of energy. The best time to eat before you exercise varies from one to three hours. Basically, it depends on several __________ such as the type and amount of food as well as body size, age, and gender.
questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 음식 종류와 양, 체구, 나이, 성별 같은 여러 요소에 달려 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ factors: '요소들'. such as 뒤에 구체적 예시가 나열.
❌ ① outcomes(결과): 원인이 아닌 결과.
❌ ② symptoms(증상): 의학적 증상이 아님.
❌ ④ exercises(운동): 음식/체구/나이는 운동이 아님.
det.tip: factor: 요소, 요인 / depend on factors: 요소에 달려 있다

questions.passage: This can cause <u>various</u> stomach issues. When you eat, blood rushes to the digestive system to help break down the food and absorb its nutrients.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 <u>various</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 이는 다양한 위장 문제를 일으킬 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② diverse(다양한): various와 동의어.
❌ ① identical(동일한): 반대.
❌ ③ rare(드문): 다른 의미.
❌ ④ minor(사소한): 다른 의미.
det.tip: various = diverse = different (다양한)

questions.passage: This happens in order to supply your muscles with the oxygen and nutrients they <u>require</u>.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 <u>require</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 근육이 필요로 하는 산소와 영양분을 공급하기 위해.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ need(필요로 하다): require와 동의어.
❌ ① reject(거부하다): 반대.
❌ ② produce(생산하다): 다른 의미.
❌ ④ waste(낭비하다): 반대.
det.tip: require = need = demand (필요로 하다)

questions.passage: For this reason, doctors <u>recommend</u> that people eat food containing carbohydrates within thirty minutes after working out.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 <u>recommend</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 의사들은 탄수화물 섭취를 권장한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② suggest(제안하다): recommend와 동의어.
❌ ① prohibit(금지하다): 반대.
❌ ③ demand(요구하다): 더 강한 뉘앙스.
❌ ④ prevent(방지하다): 다른 의미.
det.tip: recommend = suggest = advise (권장하다, 제안하다)

questions.passage: Exercising on an empty stomach can also be <u>harmful</u> and unpleasant. This is because the body needs energy to exercise.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 <u>harmful</u>과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 빈속 운동은 해로울 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② beneficial(유익한): harmful의 반의어.
❌ ① dangerous(위험한): harmful과 유사.
❌ ③ toxic(독성의): harmful과 유사.
❌ ④ damaging(손해를 주는): harmful과 유사.
det.tip: harmful = dangerous = damaging (해로운) ↔ beneficial = helpful (유익한)

questions.passage: This is because <u>intense</u> exercise uses up all the glycogen in your muscles. Some people end up suffering from nausea and headaches.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 <u>intense</u>와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 강한 운동이 근육의 모든 글리코겐을 다 써버린다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ mild(가벼운, 온화한): intense의 반의어.
❌ ① vigorous(활발한): intense와 유사.
❌ ② strenuous(격렬한): intense와 유사.
❌ ④ severe(심한): intense와 유사.
det.tip: intense = vigorous = strenuous (강렬한, 격렬한) ↔ mild = gentle = light (가벼운)

questions.passage:
(A) When you eat, blood rushes to the digestive system to help break <u>down</u> the food.

(B) The old building was torn <u>down</u> to make room for the new park.
questions.stem: 위 (A)와 (B)의 밑줄 친 down의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 음식을 분해하기 위해 (break down = 분해하다) (B) 오래된 건물을 허물었다 (tear down = 허물다)
det.analysis: ✅ ① (A) break down: 분해하다 (B) tear down: 허물다. 둘 다 down이 '완전히' 뉘앙스.
det.tip: break down: 분해하다 / tear down: 허물다 / down의 다양한 용법: 아래로, 완전히

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?
"to take in food or nutrients through the body's systems"

det.korean: "신체 기관을 통해 음식이나 영양분을 받아들이다" → 흡수하다
det.analysis:
✅ ② absorb(흡수하다): 정의와 일치.
❌ ① release(방출하다): 반대.
❌ ③ reject(거부하다): 반대.
❌ ④ produce(생산하다): 다른 의미.
det.tip: absorb: 흡수하다 / absorb nutrients: 영양분을 흡수하다

questions.passage: When you eat, blood rushes to the digestive system to help break down the food and absorb its nutrients. But when you start to exercise, blood moves from the digestive system to your muscles. As a result, the __________ (digest) process is paused until the blood returns. You shouldn't exercise with a stomach full of food.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 그 결과, 소화 과정은 혈액이 돌아올 때까지 중단된다.
det.analysis: ✅ digestion: digest(동사) → digestion(명사). process를 수식하는 명사 필요 (명사+명사 복합어).
det.tip: digest(v. 소화하다) → digestion(n. 소화) → digestive(adj. 소화의)

questions.passage: Your blood sugar levels are low, and you don't have enough glycogen stored in your body. If you exercise on an empty stomach, you will most likely lack energy and feel __________ (unusual) tired. There can also be more serious outcomes.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 빈속에 운동하면 에너지가 부족하고 유난히 피곤해진다.
det.analysis: ✅ unusually: unusual(형용사) → unusually(부사). tired(형용사)를 수식하는 부사 필요.
det.tip: unusual(adj. 이례적인) → unusually(adv. 유난히, 이례적으로) / 부사가 형용사 수식

questions.passage: I worked out right after dinner and got a stomachache. Why did that happen? Well, the problem is that you __________. This can cause various stomach issues. When you eat, blood rushes to the digestive system to help break down the food.
questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: ① ate too little food for dinner
② drank too much water before exercising
④ exercised too soon after eating

det.korean: 문제는 식사 후 너무 빨리 운동한 것이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 식사 후 너무 빨리 운동: exercised too soon after eating.
❌ ①③④ 본문에 없는 이유.
det.tip: too soon after eating: 식사 후 너무 빨리 / cause stomach issues: 위장 문제를 일으키다

questions.passage: For this reason, doctors recommend that people eat food containing carbohydrates within thirty minutes after working out. This replaces the muscle glycogen you have lost. If you weigh 60 kilograms, you should try to consume between 60 and 90 grams of carbohydrates after you exercise. This is equal to about __________.
questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: ① two steaks or five eggs
② a glass of milk or an apple
③ one bowl of white rice or three bananas
④ five slices of bread or two pizzas

det.korean: 이는 대략 흰 쌀밥 한 그릇 또는 바나나 세 개와 동일하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② one bowl of white rice or three bananas: 원문 그대로.
❌ ①③④ 본문에 없는 음식.
det.tip: 60~90g of carbohydrates ≈ 흰 쌀밥 1그릇 ≈ 바나나 3개
